notes: Credit: the ship's shape is traced from the owner's references, a shuttle concept by PAUL (zana), found online, through a drawing made from it. The references and the drawing stay out of the repository and off any public page; only these numbers are kept here.

Locked by the owner on 2026-10-14 (plan v7): the whole outline from the drawing's top view, the heights from its side view, drawn at 31 m (the hangar's keep-out estimate of 2026-10-07, never his); cockpit height 1.8 to 2.4 m.
Frame: metres; y from the nose spike's tip back to the stern, x across (starboard positive, the side ring's side), z up from the ground the ship stands on.

Built at 46 m (2026-10-18, PRD #10: the owner asked for a much bigger ship, the length the overseer's call on his delegation): every number in this file is drawn at drawn_length and is scaled by length / drawn_length where the ship is built (tools/props/library/inside/ship_outline.py); the hangar is sized to the ship.
made: 2026-10-14, v7: the whole outline as drawn; the stern airlock; the engines the side tubes

leg_pairs.from: plan v7's side page (plan-side.png): the two landing legs under the belly, one pair forward, one aft

rooms.name: cockpit
rooms.for: flying the ship: two pilot seats with the flight stick and consoles under the nose windows; take-off, landing and flight
rooms.notes: in the drawn front, as wide as the hull is there; the windshield slopes over the seats

rooms.name: crew quarters
rooms.for: sleep: four bunks in two stacks (orange padded), lockers; save and skip time

rooms.name: navigation room
rooms.for: navigation systems: the star map and route plotting between the Moon and Mars

rooms.name: galley
rooms.for: food: eat and prepare meals (counter, food stores, a table with fold-down seats)

rooms.name: storage
rooms.for: storage: cargo racks and crates for the base's supplies and parts

rooms.name: engine and power room
rooms.for: engines and power: the power core, fuel and the controls of the two main engines either side of the airlock behind it; repairs
rooms.notes: its floor steps up 0.4 m at 23.5 m over the belly rising toward the stern; the way to the airlock

rooms.name: airlock
rooms.for: the one way in and out, and the dock (the owner, 2026-10-14: the dark block at the stern is the airlock; docking and boarding are one thing): an inner door from the engine room, an outer hatch through the stern face
rooms.notes: inside the drawn dark block (3.65 m wide): a chamber 3.0 m wide on a floor 2.4 m up (the belly rises under the stern), its outer hatch reached through the block's narrowing tail to the stern face

walkway.name: walkway
walkway.notes: the corridor joining every compartment, cockpit to engine room; it widens into a short forward hall between y 12.0 and 12.8 behind the cockpit

thrusters.name: main engine
thrusters.for: flight: the two ribbed tubes either side of the airlock block, set into the hull as drawn (his painting's white round pods at the back)

thrusters.name: lift thruster
thrusters.for: vertical take-off and landing: set into the belly, two forward, two aft

thrusters.name: nose thruster
thrusters.for: turning: small thrusters in the drawn nose plate, each side, under and over

side_ring.name: side ring
side_ring.label: docking hatch and people airlock
side_ring.notes: the drawing's and his painting's ring on the hull's side: the docking hatch, and the people airlock too, one opening for both, round and sized for a person (1.9 m across, its sill 0.1 m over the deck), in a collar standing out of the hull (the owner on 2026-10-14, after the record that called it hull detail, which was wrong; PRD #10 comment of 2026-10-18)

windows.from: plan v7's side page: the nose windows over the cockpit
